newsitem.title: UK: Romania ratings affirmed by S&P.
newsitem.headline: Romania ratings affirmed by S&P.

text.p: Credit ratings for the Republic of Romania, which is undergoing key structural economic reforms, were affirmed by Standard & Poor's on Tuesday.

S&P affirmed Romania's BB minus foreign currency and BBB minus local currency long-term ratings. The outlook on the ratings was stable, reflecting expectations the new political leadership wanted to address structural problems.

"Failure to adhere to the ambitious austerity programme -- a possibility given the potential for negative social reactions as the programme requires tough and unpopular measures -- and secure international support would likely result in downward credit pressure," S&P said.

The agency said Romania's ratings were constrained by a fragile liquidity position with foreign exchange reserve coverage of the financing gap at a very low 11 percent at year end 1996 and significant structural weaknesses in the economy.
Other factors included last year's imprudent pre-election economic management, with an increase in the central bank's quasi-fiscal activity, and weak public finances.

But improved prospects for tighter financial policies, and the anticipated resumption of International Monetary Fund and World Bank lending, supported the ratings. S&P said this would improve Romania's liquidity position and support key reforms.
